hero.headline: Worried about the fires? Get a straight answer for your address.
hero.lede: Fire Watch checks the data professionals use — satellite hotspots, active incidents, fire weather — against your location in Portugal. You get one color, the reason behind it, and at most three actions. If the answer is that you're fine, it says so plainly.
hero.verdictNote: Every briefing opens with one of these four words and the single reason behind it. Green is a real answer too — it means you can stop refreshing the news.

crisis.title: Spain and France are burning. Portugal shares the fuel and the weather.
crisis.lede: In the 24 hours before this update, satellites logged 264 confident fire detections across Iberia and southern France: an active front in Castellón (Spain), fire clusters in the Gironde forests (France), and detections in northern Portugal's Trás-os-Montes.
crisis.emergency: If you can see flames or smoke from your home, or Civil Protection has told you to leave — don't wait for a briefing. Call 112 and follow ANEPC instructions. This service is for the step before that: worried, but not in immediate danger.

crisis.kicker: Most fires on the news never threaten any given home — distance, wind direction, and terrain decide. But “probably fine” is a guess. A briefing replaces the guess with a checked answer for your address.

report.title: Four answers, in this order.
report.lede: A briefing is built to be read at 11pm by someone who is not fine. Verdict first, reasoning second, no decimal probabilities.

deliverables.title: Is my home threatened right now?
deliverables.text: The verdict — Green, Yellow, Orange, or Red — and the one factor that put it there.

deliverables.title: Where is the danger, and which way is it moving?
deliverables.text: Every relevant fire mapped with distance and wind alignment. A fire 15 km downwind is ruled out explicitly; a smaller one upwind is not.

deliverables.title: What should I do?
deliverables.text: At most three actions matched to the level — including “nothing tonight”, when that's the honest answer.

deliverables.title: What would change this answer?
deliverables.text: The exact conditions that would escalate or downgrade the verdict — so you know what to watch instead of watching everything.

report.delivery: Delivered as a PDF and your own report page. Every number traces to an evidence bundle stored at run time.

data.title: The same sources the professionals watch.
data.lede: One national data sweep per assessment, stored so every figure in your report can be checked afterwards. Nothing is hand-picked.

sources.name: IPMA RCM
sources.detail: Portugal's official fire-danger index for your municipality, 1–5, refreshed hourly.

sources.name: NASA FIRMS
sources.detail: VIIRS and MODIS thermal hotspots, confidence-filtered. Typically 1–4 hours behind reality — the report says so.

sources.name: National incident feed
sources.detail: Every active wildfire in Portugal with crews, vehicles, and aircraft committed — including how stretched the national response already is.

sources.name: Fire weather
sources.detail: High-resolution IPMA forecasts. Dry + hot + windy raises the score even when no fire is near.

sources.name: EFFIS
sources.detail: The EU's calibrated fire-weather scale, as forecast context on top of the national rating.

sources.name: MeteoAlarm
sources.detail: Official heat and wind warnings from national authorities.

data.note: If a source is down, the report says which one and what that does to confidence. Detection latency and data gaps are stated, not papered over.

method.title: A sensor and an analyst — separated on purpose.
method.lede: A deterministic engine scores the risk; an analyst layer explains it. Same inputs, same verdict — judgment is added on top and labeled, never mixed in.

engine.title: The engine senses and scores
points: Fetches all sources and stores the raw evidence.
Scores five dimensions: active-fire threat, fire weather, fuel, property vulnerability, escape routes.
Applies hard overrides — a close upwind fire forces the level up regardless of the average.

analyst.title: The analyst interprets
points: Reads the threat as a trajectory: where fire will be given wind, fuel, and slope — not just where it is.
Writes the narrative and actions in plain language.
Disagreement with the computed level appears as a labeled note, never silently.

principles.title: Verdict first
principles.text: The color and its reason lead. Detail follows for those who want it.

principles.title: No false precision
principles.text: Four levels, stated assumptions. Decimals don't help you decide whether to load the car.

principles.title: Auditable
principles.text: “0 incidents within 60 km” is checkable against the evidence recorded for that run.

flow.title: Message the agent. Answer a few questions. Get your briefing.
flow.lede: The whole exchange is a chat with the agent. No forms, no account.

steps.title: Message the agent
steps.text: On Telegram. You'll be asked to verify who you are.

steps.title: Get approved
steps.text: Access is personal — the operator approves each requester before a report runs.

steps.title: Answer a few questions
steps.text: Your address or coordinates in Portugal; optionally structure type, cleared distance, escape routes. Skipped answers become stated assumptions.

steps.title: Receive your briefing
steps.text: A plain-language summary in the chat, the PDF, and your report page. Valid as of its timestamp; refresh on request.
